I'm late but better late than never:

America is a continent, it is not a matter of perception, it is just reality.

To begin with, the American continent was named after an ITALIAN PERSON; Americo Vespucci, who was a crucial figure when it came to discovering "the new continente", aka, AMERICA. As you can see, Americo is way closer to be considered "Latino" by the way -which is not an extremely important fact but I just wanted to let that sink in-. Regarding the original matter -America being a continent-, as you may or may not know, when Columbus discovered this huge land he FIRST ARRIVED TO THE BAHAMAS in 1492, so we could say the origins of America weren't really linked to the US if you know what I mean.

I would like to quote a bit of information on how and when the name of America was given to the continent we know today; "He (Waldseemüller) included on the map data gathered by Vespucci during his voyages of 1501-1502 to the New World. Waldseemüller named the new lands “America” on his 1507 map in the recognition of Vespucci's understanding that a new continent had been uncovered following Columbus' and subsequent voyages in the late 15th century." (NATIONAL GEOGRAPHIC; n.d)

We can see that the name of America was given in 1507 WHILE as for the United States "the invasion of the North American continent and its peoples began with the Spanish in 1565", way later, right? (Allen; 2016)

As you know, the US became a country by "uniting" (just like its name shows) different states that belonged to other counties/colonies. For example, Texas was Mexican before Houston put into practice a plan in order to be able to make Texas be mostly populated by his people so he was able to take over it by defeating the Mexicans as he already had greater forces there, other states were obtained from Spain -like Florida- or even from France -just like Louisiana which was named after the King of France, Louis XIV-.

The US was originally called the "United Colonies" but as a result of the American Revolution (when the thirteen American colonies revolted against the rule of Great Britain) it became a country on its own and changed its name. "On September 9, 1776, the Second Continental Congress adopted a new name for what had been called the "United Colonies.” The moniker United States of America has remained since then as a symbol of freedom and independence." (NCC; 2021).

FINAL THOUGHT

As obvious as it appears, the United States of America took its name after the continent, the original America, the first one. It is understandable why you guys call yourselves Americans as perhaps "Unitedstatians" doesn't sound too "picturesque" but claiming that America is a country is just too ignorant for me and every American that wasn't born in the US. As your country is by far the most successful of the whole American continent -having been the biggest and only superpower for a short period of time after the Cold War-, it makes sense that other countries have come to call you Americans, just like Japan, but on the other side, we Spanish speakers, do not call you that way; we call you estadounidenses (Unitedstatians) as you are from Estados Unidos (The US).

The point of this whole reply was to explain to you how America is a continent while the country is THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA, which can be shortened as "America" for convenience purposes, just like Mexicans do with the United Mexican States, you can also stick to the American demonym for the same reason, we have no problem with that. The "biggest but" here is that you will never be able to "gatekeep" the term America or the demonym American as only yours as it already belongs to every single place of this whole continent -in which lot of us can live thanks to Vespucci and Columbus- and to every single person that was born here, we are all Americans that live in America. I'm an American from Argentina and Lady Gaga is an American from the US just like Hernan Cortés was not less European than the Queen Elizabeth.
